source.description: Project parser entry that consumes the attacker-controlled OpenFlow flow-mod string supplied by the target input.

sink.description: Second minimatch_destroy() on fm.match after ofctl_parse_flows__() already destroyed the same minimatch.

root_cause.description: The target cleanup destroys fm.match after handing the same fm to ofctl_parse_flows__(), whose loop already destroys fm->match.

taint_source.code: char *error = parse_ofp_str(fm, command, string, port_map, table_map,
taint_source.description: The parser consumes the attacker-controlled flow string. The OSS-Fuzz target obtains it from PoC bytes and passes it into this project parser.

tainted_value_origin.description: Successful parsing materializes fm->match, including heap-owned minimatch flow storage that must be destroyed exactly once.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled flow string is parsed into an ofputil_flow_mod.
Parsing initializes fm->match and allocates minimatch flow storage.
The helper encodes the parsed flow and destroys fm->match in its cleanup loop.
The caller then destroys fm.match again, causing a double-free.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The PoC-derived flow string is parsed by OVS into an ofputil_flow_mod. Successful parsing initializes fm.match and allocates minimatch flow storage. The fuzz target passes &fm to ofctl_parse_flows__(), whose cleanup loop frees fm->ofpacts and destroys fm->match. Control then returns to ofctl_parse_flow(), which calls minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) again on the same object, causing a double-free.
root_cause_analysis.why_patch_works: The patch moves cleanup into a single free path in ofctl_parse_flows__() and removes the extra minimatch_destroy(&fm.match) from ofctl_parse_flow(). The helper now cleans each flow mod once, including early no-protocol exits, so fm.match is destroyed exactly once.
